```{r setup}
s <- read.csv("../results/summary.csv")
f3 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3); f2 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2)
nv <- s[s$method == "naive", ]; mp <- s[s$method == "midpoint", ]; ic <- s[s$method == "interval", ]
fit <- stats::lm(bias ~ predicted, data = nv, weights = 1 / nv$mcse^2)
dd <- nv[abs(nv$d1 - nv$d2) >= 2, ]
eq <- nv[nv$d1 == nv$d2, ]; eqd <- eq[abs(eq$predicted) > 0.05, ]
old <- setwd(".."); source("R/00-model.R"); setwd(old)
tr <- c(m8 = rmst_true(11) - rmst_true(8), m16 = rmst_true(19) - rmst_true(16))
w3 <- 3 * mp$mcse
```

# Abstract {.unnumbered}

**Background.** Progression is detected at scheduled visits, so a recorded event time
is the first visit after the event. When two trials in an unanchored comparison use
different schedules, the recording delay differs between the arms. Catalog problem
OUT-14 asks how much this biases a transported restricted mean survival time (RMST)
difference.

**Methods.** Two single arms of 300, Weibull event times, visit spacing 0 (continuous),
1, 2 or 3 months in trial A and 0 or 3 months in trial B, two event rates and two true
differences: 32 scenarios, 1000 replicates each. RMST at 24 months from Kaplan-Meier on
recorded times, Kaplan-Meier after moving events back half a spacing, and an
interval-censored Weibull model.

**Results.** Treating recorded times as exact biased the RMST difference by
$(d_B/2)F_B(\tau) - (d_A/2)F_A(\tau)$ (simulated against predicted slope
`r f3(coef(fit)[[2]])`), up to `r f2(max(abs(dd$bias)))` months where the schedules
differed by 2 months or more. The true difference was `r f2(tr[["m8"]])` or
`r f2(tr[["m16"]])` months. The midpoint shift and the interval-censored model reduced
the bias to at most `r f3(max(abs(mp$bias)))` and `r f3(max(abs(ic$bias)))` months.

**Conclusion.** A 3-month difference in visit spacing produces a spurious RMST
difference of the same size as a real treatment effect. Covariate balancing cannot
remove it because it acts on the time axis. Move events to the interval midpoint or fit
an interval-censored model.

# The problem {#sec-problem}

An event in $(v_{k-1}, v_k]$ is recorded at $v_k$, on average $d/2$ late. RMST up to
$\tau$ [@royston2013] accumulates the delay for every event before $\tau$, so treating
recorded times as exact inflates it by about $(d/2)F(\tau)$. DESIGN.md gave $d/2$ without
the factor $F(\tau)$. Within one trial the delay is shared by both arms and nearly
cancels. Across trials with different spacing it enters the contrast, and weighting on
covariates does not act on it.

# Design {#sec-design}

Registered protocol: `protocol.md`; ADEMP structure [@morris2019]. Weibull shape 1.2; A's
median 8 or 16 months, B's median equal or 3 months longer; dropout uniform on 12 to 60
months; administrative censoring at 36 months; $\tau = 24$. Recorded times are used
directly, which is what an ideal reconstruction of published curves returns. The
interval-censored Weibull model treats each event as lying between the previous and
the recorded visit; it is correctly specified here, which favors it.

# Results {#sec-results}

![Bias of the RMST difference against the predicted naive bias, with 95% Monte Carlo intervals.](figures/fig1-bias.png){#fig-bias}

The naive bias followed the prediction across all scenarios (@fig-bias), with either
sign depending on which trial had the coarser schedule. With no true difference, a
3-month schedule in one trial alone produced an apparent difference of
`r f2(nv$bias[nv$d1 == 0 & nv$d2 == 3 & nv$median_A == 8 & nv$effect == 0])` months. With
A's median 16 months and a true difference of `r f2(tr[["m16"]])` months, a 3-month
schedule in A alone removed `r f2(-nv$bias[nv$d1 == 3 & nv$d2 == 0 & nv$median_A == 16 & nv$effect == 3])`
months of it. With equal schedules the bias was near zero where the arms
had equal event probabilities; it was `r f3(eqd$bias[1])` and `r f3(eqd$bias[2])` where
they did not (predicted `r f3(eqd$predicted[1])` and `r f3(eqd$predicted[2])`), so
the registered control, which assumed zero there, failed in `r nrow(eqd)` of `r nrow(eq)`
cells for a reason the mechanism predicts.

The midpoint shift left bias within 3 MCSE of zero in `r sum(abs(mp$bias) <= w3)` of
`r nrow(mp)` scenarios and the interval-censored model in
`r sum(abs(ic$bias) <= 3 * ic$mcse)` of `r nrow(ic)`; the remaining bias was below 0.1
month.

# What this does not answer {#sec-limits}

The binary event-by-time endpoint and comparisons with different maximum follow-up
were not run. Reconstruction error from digitized curves was not simulated. Visits were
exactly on schedule; real visit windows add jitter that the midpoint shift ignores.
Peer review has not been done.
